Proton Fights for Privacy as Linux Age Verification Expands
recent_posts.summary: Proton CEO Andy Yen has published a blog post arguing that current age verification proposals worldwide threaten online anonymity and privacy. He acknowledges that protecting children online is a real concern, but warns that broad age verification mandates would effectively end anonymous internet use. Key arguments include: collected identity data inevitably gets leaked (citing Discord's 70,000-user breach and the EU/UK age verification app being bypassed within hours), third-party age verification companies face incentives to monetize user data, and big tech companies like Apple and Google cannot be trusted as gatekeepers given their history of data exploitation. Yen also calls out Meta for lobbying in favor of age verification not to protect children, but to offload responsibility. If age verification must exist, Proton argues it should be client-side only, use no facial scans or uploaded IDs, be fully anonymized, end-to-end encrypted, and built on open source code. The post also touches on how these laws could extend beyond age to nationality-based internet blocking.

recent_posts.title: How to Dual Boot Windows 11 and Ubuntu 26.04 LTS
recent_posts.summary: Step-by-step guide to dual booting Ubuntu 26.04 LTS alongside Windows 10/11. Covers downloading the Ubuntu ISO, flashing it to a USB drive with Balena Etcher, shrinking the Windows C partition using Disk Management to free up space, configuring BIOS boot order and disabling Secure Boot, running the Ubuntu installer with manual partitioning (ext4, root mount point), setting up the GRUB bootloader, and verifying both OSes boot correctly. Also includes post-install tips like installing VLC, GIMP, LibreOffice, and Steam.

recent_posts.title: Disable YouTube Shorts in YOUR Feed
recent_posts.summary: YouTube has added a new method to disable Shorts from your feed on mobile. By navigating to Settings > Time Management and setting the daily limit to 0 minutes, you can prevent Shorts from appearing in your feed. You may need to refresh or tap a Short once before the change takes effect.

recent_posts.title: US bill HR8250 would require age verification at the operating system level
recent_posts.summary: US Congress bill HR8250, the Parents Decide Act, introduced April 13th 2026, would require operating system providers to verify the age of every user and mandate parental involvement for users under 18. The bill's definitions of 'operating system' and 'operating system provider' are broadly worded, potentially covering not just iOS, Android, and Windows but also Linux, open-source projects, car infotainment systems, smart TVs, and embedded devices. Enforcement would fall under the FTC. Key concerns include the end of anonymous device use, mandatory identity data collection tied to real-world attributes, vague language leaving wide regulatory interpretation to the FTC, and implications for open-source contributors and distributors. Viewers are encouraged to contact their representatives.

top_posts.title: Zorin OS 18 reaches 2 million downloads as Windows users migrate to Linux
top_posts.summary: Zorin OS 18 has reached 2 million downloads in under three months, with over 75% coming from Windows users. The Linux distribution is gaining traction as Windows 10 reaches end-of-life and Windows 11's strict hardware requirements (TPM 2.0, newer CPUs) block many older PCs. Zorin OS appeals to Windows switchers through familiar layouts, Windows app compatibility via Wine, and features like OneDrive integration. The project is expanding with Zorin Grid for IT management in organizations, positioning itself as a viable alternative for both individual users and enterprises looking to extend the life of older hardware.

top_posts.title: Linus Torvalds defends Rust integration in Linux kernel despite maintainer friction
top_posts.summary: Linus Torvalds discusses the ongoing integration of Rust into the Linux kernel, acknowledging the friction and maintainer pushback it has created over the past five years. He defends the decision as necessary to prevent kernel stagnation and attract new contributors, noting his role has shifted from saying 'no' to encouraging maintainers to embrace new ideas. While Rust has generated controversy including maintainer resignations and debates over code review processes, Torvalds believes the disruption is worthwhile and that Rust is finally transitioning from experimental to a real part of the kernel, though it took longer than expected.

top_posts.title: Ubuntu repository outage causes days of package installation failures
top_posts.summary: Ubuntu's package repositories experienced a 35-minute outage that caused days of disruption for users worldwide. The archive.ubuntu.com and security.ubuntu.com repositories went down, preventing package installations and security updates. While the servers came back online quickly, the resulting backlog overwhelmed mirrors and caused ongoing failures for several days. The incident highlighted critical infrastructure weaknesses in Ubuntu's centralized repository system and raised questions about redundancy, failover mechanisms, and community communication during outages.

top_posts.title: Firefox faces backlash after controversial terms of service update
top_posts.summary: Firefox is facing backlash for its new terms of service, which many feel violate user privacy. Zoran OS has dropped Firefox as their default browser, citing privacy concerns. Prominent YouTubers are also moving away from Firefox. With Chrome and Edge known for data collection, Brave is suggested as a privacy-friendly alternative. Mozilla could face funding issues if Google withdraws their $500 million support.

top_posts.title: Caligra C100 developer terminal announced with retro design and custom Linux OS
top_posts.summary: The Caligra C100 is a new Linux-based developer terminal with a retro wedge chassis design reminiscent of Commodore 64. It features AMD Ryzen 9 9440HS processor, 96GB DDR5 RAM, 1TB SSD, and mechanical keyboard, priced at $2,000 with $99 pre-order deposit. The device runs a custom Linux OS called Workbench, marketed as distraction-free for creators and technical work. However, the product lacks clear differentiation, detailed specifications about the OS, and concrete use cases, making its target audience and value proposition unclear compared to competitors like Framework, System76, or standard Linux workstations.
